rationale: Z-p22 (2026-10-04). A container member's `scope`/`ownerName` was the container's BARE name, while the shared projection spells a symbol `scope ? scope + '.' + name : name` (pool-worker.ts:930) — so a container published its ABSOLUTE name and its members published a RELATIVE one. Measured on ghostty/pkg/macos/iosurface/iosurface.zig:10: container `IOSurface.Error`, member published as `Error.InvalidOperation`, and the `contains` edge's source `Error` is not a published qualified name anywhere in the file. Over the published 3,834-file draw `sha256:2f3545f9` that was 15,686 of 80,876 `contains` edges (19.4%) in 421 files; after the change 99.99% are composition-resolvable and 8 are not (a shared-file `keepSymbol` denylist, not this analyzer). The rows are grouped by what each one can catch. DEPTH-2 rows catch a mutant that reverts to `container.name`. DEPTH-3 (`Registry.Entry.Slot.value`) catches a mutant that qualifies by exactly ONE level, which passes every depth-2 row. `Chdr`/`Elf64.Chdr` catches a mutant that picks a wrong-but-existing container: zig/lib/std/elf.zig declares `Elf32.Chdr`, `Elf64.Chdr` and a file-scope alias `Chdr`, so the bare name names three real declarations. The file-scope rows (`Point`, `Shape`, `Color`) are the negative half — a top-level container's path EQUALS its bare name, so these are byte-identical to the pre-fix output, and a mutant that prefixes or over-qualifies cannot produce them. `locals()` pins Z22's refusal, which a mutant widening the path logic to every enclosing node would break. The quoted row pins the join: `canonicalizePublishedNames` strips quoting from `ownerName` but not from `scope`, so the path is built from stripped components — building it from raw lexer text would spell the container `my type` and the member `@"my type".field`, the exact split this change removes.

expectRelationships.note: Z-p22: the member's owner is the container's ABSOLUTE path, and `Elf64.Chdr` is the qualified name the container itself publishes. Pre-fix this edge's source was `Chdr`, a name three declarations in this file hold (Elf32.Chdr, Elf64.Chdr, and a file-scope alias).
a METHOD is a container member too, so the function branch reads the same path
depth 3: a mutant that qualifies by exactly one level fails here and passes every depth-2 row
the error-set member branch reads the container's name directly, so it is a second site the fix had to reach; this is the measured corpus site
a FILE-SCOPE container's path equals its bare name: this edge is byte-identical before and after the fix, which is what keeps the change off the top-level majority

the path is built from STRIPPED components: `canonicalizePublishedNames` strips quoting from ownerName but not from scope, so a raw `@"my type"` component would spell the member `@"my type".field` while the container spells `my type`
a quoted FIELD name is stripped on both halves, so the edge target and the member's qualified name agree

forbidRelationships.note: Z-p22: the pre-fix spelling. `Chdr` names three real declarations in this file, so an edge to it binds by a rule nobody chose
and this source is not a published qualified name AT ALL — the failure the fix removes
a one-level qualification of a depth-3 path
the target is the member's BARE name; a dotted target would not compose with the source
Z22: a container declared inside a FUNCTION body has no stable identity, so none of its declarations is a symbol and no contains edge is emitted for it
and the path fix does not widen that refusal — the container is not published, so nothing can own its members
